events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The Southwest Clean Air Agency has continued an Air Quality
Advisory, which is in effect until 11 PM PDT Thursday.

An Air Quality Advisory for smoke remains in effect for Lewis County.
Wildfires burning in the region combined with forecasted conditions
will cause air quality to reach unhealthy levels due to smoke at
times through 11 PM PDT Thursday.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems. Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

More information about air quality can be found at:
www.swcleanair.gov

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: King, WA; Kitsap, WA; Mason, WA; Pierce, WA; Snohomish, WA; Thurston, WA
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
An Air Quality Alert for Smoke has been issued by the following
agencies until 8 AM PDT Friday: Puget Sound Clean Air Agency and
Olympic Region Clean Air Agency.

An Air Quality Alert has been extended for King, Kitsap, Mason, Pierce,
Snohomish, and Thurston counties through 8 AM Friday, August 7 due
to wildfire smoke from regional fires.

Air quality is MODERATE to UNHEALTHY for most of the area and is
expected to gradually improve Thursday and overnight. Improvement in
the Cascades will lag behind, and parts may remain UNHEALTHY FOR
SENSITIVE GROUPS through Friday mid-day.

When the air quality is UNHEALTHY FOR SENSITIVE GROUPS, individuals
with health concerns and pre-existing conditions should reduce
exposure and take precautions.

At UNHEALTHY air quality, all individuals should take precautions to
reduce exposure. This means limiting time outside, avoiding
strenuous outdoor activity, and following tips for cleaner indoor
air.

Visit pscleanair.gov and orcaa.org/news-notices for current
conditions, updates, and more information.
